title: Constructible devissage: the thick-subcategory generation
statement:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type scheme over $k$ and $A$ a
finite coefficient ring as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions].
The triangulated category $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ is the thick subcategory of
$D(X,A)$ generated by the objects

$$
Rg_*j_!L ,
$$

where $U$ is a locally closed stratum of $X$,
$j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$ is the open immersion into its closure,
$g:\overline U\hookrightarrow X$ is the closed immersion, and $L$ is a lisse
sheaf of $A$-modules on $U$ with flat stalks. Constant coefficients
$L=A_U$ do not suffice in general.

proof.text: The finite coefficient ring A=O_E/(varpi_E)^n is annihilated by l^n. Indeed spectralNorm_extends and the p-adic norm of l show |l|_E<1. The maximal ideal membership clause of Padic.extension_integers_dvr therefore puts l in m_E. The same theorem identifies the ideal generated by the chosen uniformizer with m_E; hence l^n is in m_E^n, the defining coefficient ideal. The quotient map kills l^n, and n is positive by the coefficient convention.

source.place: Proof Steps 0–2, finite coefficient hypothesis for the flat-model generation theorem

proof.text: Equip X with its given structure morphism over Spec k and specialize proEtaleThickGeneration_eq of [sk-lem-sf-flat-model] to A, using its finite coefficient-ring instance and the preceding annihilation. Its closure generators are definitionally sfProEtaleClosureGenerators, with the actual scheme-theoretic closure factorization. The only remaining difference is boundedness: a finite set of nonzero cohomology degrees has integer lower and upper bounds, while the degrees between any two integer bounds form a finite set. Reassociate the constructibility, boundedness and finite-Tor conjunctions. This proves the generation equality without repeating the flat-model, filtration and comparison proof of the existing theorem.

proof.text: Choose the concrete coefficient datum with base field the algebraic closure of F_5, ell=3, coefficient extension Q_3 itself, and level one. Use the identity scheme as X_0 in the trace-formula conventions, which need not be the witness X. The coefficient quotient ideal at level one is the maximal ideal by the existing DVR theorem, so the quotient is nonzero. The spectral norm puts 3 in that ideal; primality gives characteristic three. Algebraic closures and ULift supply the stated universes without changing these facts.

Take X=Spec k[t,t^-1]. It is affine and separated over k, and its structure map is locally of finite type because polynomial k maps finitely to its localization away from t (an open immersion) and polynomial k is finite type over k. Apply [lem-trf-kummer-monodromy] to obtain an exact additive fibre functor F, a natural endomorphism t and a generator L[0] with t_L nonnilpotent and with t zero on every constant stratum extension.

By [lem-trf-nilpotent-fiber-homology], the class Q of complexes whose F-cohomology has nilpotent t in every degree is triangulated and stable under retracts. A constant stratum extension in degree zero is in Q: t is zero on its degree-zero homology, and every other homology vanishes. Naturality transports nilpotence across isomorphisms, so all objects of trfConstantClosureGenerators are in Q. The universal property of triangEnvelope [pur9-def-thick] puts their thick closure in Q.

Let K=L[0]. Since it is a lisse-flat closure generator, the generation equality from Step 2 puts K in D^b_ctf(X,A). If K were in the constant-generated thick closure it would be in Q by the preceding step. The canonical degree-zero homology isomorphism H^0(L[0])=L would then make t_L nilpotent, contradicting the Kummer witness. These T, X and K prove the existential counterexample with the original signature.
